q: Consider the rural local government amendment: 1-It was passed in 1992. 2-It came into force in 1993. 3-It transferred twenty-nine subjects to panchayats. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The Schedule is a list of subjects a State legislature may devolve; nothing was transferred by the amendment.
why: The operative words empower a State to endow panchayats with such powers as may be necessary, which is a choice and not a transfer.
trapnote: The amendment created structures. Devolution of subjects remained a State policy choice.

q: On reservation for women in panchayats, which statement is correct?
options: Not less than one-half of seats and of chairperson offices is reserved
Not less than one-third of seats, chairperson offices being outside the reservation
Not less than one-third of seats and of chairperson offices is reserved
Not less than one-third of seats, the reservation applying only at village level
expl: The floor covers both seats and offices of chairperson at every level.
why: Andhra Pradesh provides one-half by State law, which is above the constitutional floor and not a substitute for it.
trapnote: The floor is one-third and covers chairperson offices too. States may go higher by their own law.

q: A State with a population of fifteen lakhs proposes a two-tier structure. Which statement is correct?
options: Impermissible: three tiers are mandatory in every State without exception
Permissible: a State not exceeding twenty lakhs may omit the district level
Permissible: any State may omit a tier with the approval of the Governor
Permissible: a State not exceeding twenty lakhs may omit the intermediate level
expl: The exemption is confined to the intermediate level and to States within the population limit.
why: The third option changes which tier may be omitted, which is the finer of the two available variations.
trapnote: The omission is of the intermediate tier only, and only below the population threshold.

q: Consider the two Schedules relating to local government: 1-The rural Schedule lists twenty-nine subjects. 2-The urban Schedule lists eighteen functions. 3-Both Schedules bind the State legislature to devolve them. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Neither Schedule is binding; both are lists of what may be devolved.
why: Twenty-nine and eighteen are the figures, and the non-binding character is the substantive point.
trapnote: Two figures and one principle: the Schedules enumerate, the State legislature decides.

q: Which body conducts elections to panchayats and municipalities?
options: The State Election Commission, under a distinct constitutional provision
The Election Commission of India, which supervises all elections in the country
The State Election Commission, under a law made by Parliament
The district collector, acting under the directions of the State government
expl: A separate State Election Commission is constituted under its own provision.
why: The second option is the commonest institutional confusion in the whole topic.
trapnote: Two commissions, two provisions. Local polls never go to the national commission.

q: Consider the exclusion of certain areas from the rural local government Part: 1-Fifth Schedule Scheduled Areas are excluded. 2-Certain north-eastern States are excluded. 3-The exclusion abolished the Sixth Schedule arrangements. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The exclusion protects existing arrangements rather than abolishing them.
why: The exclusion was protective: traditional systems of self-governance would have been displaced by a uniform structure.
trapnote: The exclusion protects. It does not abolish anything, and it was later bridged by a separate law.

q: On the law extending the rural local government provisions to Scheduled Areas, which statement is correct?
options: It was enacted by Parliament in 1992 and makes the Gram Panchayat the primary authority
It was enacted by each State in 1996 and makes the Gram Sabha the primary authority
It was enacted by Parliament in 1996 and makes the district council the primary authority
It was enacted by Parliament in 1996 and makes the Gram Sabha the primary authority
expl: Parliament enacted it in 1996 and the assembly of all voters is the primary authority.
why: The shift of primacy from the elected panchayat to the assembly of all voters is the defining feature of the scheme.
trapnote: Parliament, 1996, and the assembly of all voters rather than the elected body.

q: Consider the powers of the Gram Sabha in a Scheduled Area: 1-Consultation before acquisition of land. 2-Ownership of minor forest produce. 3-Trial of offences committed within the village. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The scheme confers governance and resource powers, not criminal jurisdiction.
why: Criminal trial remains with the ordinary courts; the scheme does not create a parallel judicial system.
trapnote: Governance and resources, not adjudication. No parallel criminal jurisdiction is created.

q: Consider the three categories of urban local body: 1-A transitional area has a Nagar Panchayat. 2-A smaller urban area has a Municipal Council. 3-A larger urban area has a Municipal Corporation. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: All three pairings are accurate.
why: The classification is made by the Governor having regard to population, density, revenue and other factors.
trapnote: Three categories by size. The Governor classifies, having regard to prescribed factors.

q: On the District Planning Committee, which statement is correct?
options: Not less than two-thirds of its members are elected from among elected local representatives
All its members are nominated by the State government from among officials
Not less than four-fifths of its members are elected from among elected local representatives
Not less than four-fifths of its members are nominated by the district collector
expl: At least four-fifths are elected by and from the elected members of the district panchayat and municipalities.
why: The proportion is the tested figure and the elective character is the substantive point.
trapnote: Four-fifths elected. The Committee is a body of elected representatives, not officials.

q: An election to a panchayat is challenged on grounds of irregularity. Which statement is correct?
options: It may be questioned by writ petition in the High Court at the instance of a candidate
It may be questioned before the Election Commission of India on appeal
It may be questioned by writ only where the State Election Commission declines to act
It may be questioned only by an election petition presented as State law provides
expl: Courts are barred from entertaining a challenge otherwise than by election petition.
why: The bar mirrors the corresponding provision for parliamentary and Assembly elections.
trapnote: Election petition only. The bar on court interference is express and mirrors the higher-level rule.

q: Consider the Andhra Pradesh structure: 1-The intermediate tier is the Mandal Parishad. 2-Territorial members at mandal and district level are directly elected. 3-The Mandal Parishad President is directly elected. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Territorial members are directly elected; the President and Chairperson are elected from among them.
why: Direct election at the territorial level and indirect election of the presiding offices is the pattern.
trapnote: Territorial members directly, presiding officers indirectly. Sarpanch is directly elected.

q: On the term of a panchayat and the consequences of dissolution, which statement is correct?
options: Five years, with fresh elections completed within six months of dissolution
Five years, with fresh elections completed within one year of dissolution
Six years, with fresh elections completed within six months of dissolution
Five years, the body so constituted serving a full further term of five years
expl: Five years, and elections within six months of a dissolution.
why: A body constituted on dissolution serves only the remainder of the term, which the fourth option denies.
trapnote: Two figures and one consequence: five years, six months, and only the remainder of the term.

q: Consider the State Finance Commission: 1-It is constituted every five years. 2-It reviews the financial position of local bodies. 3-Its recommendations bind the State government. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Its recommendations are advisory; the State decides with reasons.
why: The advisory character is shared with the Union Finance Commission and is frequently misstated.
trapnote: Finance Commission recommendations, Union or State, are advisory and not binding.

q: On the minimum age to contest a panchayat election, which statement is correct?
options: Eighteen years, prescribed by the Constitution itself
Twenty-five years, prescribed by the State legislature
Twenty-one years, prescribed by the State legislature
Twenty-one years, prescribed by the Constitution itself
expl: Twenty-one years is prescribed by the Constitution.
why: The voting age is eighteen and the contesting age twenty-one, which is the pair being tested.
trapnote: Vote at eighteen, contest at twenty-one. Both figures are constitutional.

q: Consider the Metropolitan Planning Committee: 1-It is constituted for areas with a population of ten lakhs or more. 2-It consolidates plans prepared by municipalities and panchayats. 3-It is constituted by the Election Commission of India. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: It is constituted under State law; the national commission has no role.
why: The third statement inserts the wrong institution, which is the recurring error in this topic.
trapnote: Planning bodies are constituted under State law. No election commission is involved.

q: Which statement about reservation for backward classes in panchayats is correct?
options: It is left to the discretion of the State legislature
It is mandatory in the same manner as for Scheduled Castes and Tribes
It is mandatory but only at the intermediate and district levels
It is prohibited, the Constitution providing for two categories only
expl: Reservation for backward classes is an enabling provision left to the State.
why: Scheduled Caste and Tribe reservation is mandatory and proportionate; backward-class reservation is not.
trapnote: Two categories are mandatory and proportionate; the third is left to the State's discretion.

q: Consider Andhra Pradesh: 1-It has twenty-six districts since April 2022. 2-Its conformity legislation for panchayats dates from 1994. 3-It has no Scheduled Areas within its territory. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The State has Scheduled Areas in several districts.
why: The presence of Scheduled Areas is what makes the 1996 extension law operative field law in the State.
trapnote: Scheduled Areas exist in the State, which is why the 1996 law matters operationally.

q: On Wards Committees in municipalities, which statement is correct?
options: They are compulsory in every municipality irrespective of population
They are compulsory where the population is ten lakhs or more
They are optional and constituted at the discretion of the State government
They are compulsory where the population is three lakhs or more
expl: The threshold is three lakhs.
why: Ten lakhs is the threshold for a different body, which is why the third option is plausible.
trapnote: Three lakhs for wards committees, ten lakhs for the metropolitan planning body.

q: Consider the two commissions relating to local bodies: 1-One conducts elections. 2-One reviews finances. 3-Both are constituted by the Governor. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: All three are accurate; both bodies are constituted by the Governor.
why: Separating the two functions between two bodies prevents the mixing of electoral and financial control.
trapnote: Two bodies, two functions, one appointing authority. The separation of functions is deliberate.
